agents.title: Agents
agents.subtitle: Versioned agent definitions (agents.md). Published versions are immutable.
agents.newSubtitle: Start from a template. The draft is validated live and can be published later.
agents.emptyText: Describe a workflow in plain language with the wizard – an agent engineer turns it into an agent.
agents.name: Name
agents.editorHint: Tab inserts spaces. Press Escape, then Tab, to leave the editor.

overview.draftText: The full runtime view appears after the first publish. Hints from the draft:

publish.title: Publish {name}?
publish.text: Publishing creates an immutable version. New events will run with it immediately.
publish.diffLabel: Changes since the last published version
publish.first: This is the first version of this agent.
publish.acknowledge: I reviewed the changes and the allowed tools.
publish.unchanged: Version {version} is already published with this content.

versions.emptyText: Publish the draft to create the first immutable version.

test.title: Test run with an example event
test.needsVersionText: Test runs execute a published version.
test.simulated: This version uses the simulated provider: deterministic, free and without outbound calls.
test.realProvider: This version calls a real provider ({providers}). The run costs money. Use provider “simulated” for free tests.
test.eventHint: Wrapped into a manual CloudEvent; you can also paste a full CloudEvent.

wizard.title: Workflow wizard
wizard.subtitle: Describe in plain language what should happen. An agent engineer reviews the result before it goes live.
wizard.created: Draft {name} created – it now waits for review.

when.title: When … happens
when.sourceHint: Sources are set up by your integrator under “Events & sources”.
when.sourceNameHint: No source exists yet – type a name; your integrator connects it later.
when.cronHint: Minute hour day month weekday, e.g. 0 9 * * 1-5

webhook.label: A system sends an event
webhook.help: Webhook, e.g. from Jira, GitHub or a scanner

manual.label: Someone starts it
manual.help: By hand or via the API

do.title: … check / do …
do.help: Write each step as you would explain it to a colleague. Pick a tool if the step needs one.
do.placeholder: e.g. Look up the CVE and rate how critical it is
do.noConnections: No connections yet – your integrator adds them under “Connections”.
do.approval: A human must approve this step before it runs

reply.title: … then reply as …
reply.help: What should come out at the end?

message.label: Message
message.help: Chat message, e.g. Teams or Slack

review.title: Name it and hand it over
review.help: Check the summary. The draft is not active until an agent engineer publishes it.
review.name: Name of the workflow
review.nameHint: Becomes the agent name, e.g. “CVE triage”.
review.classificationHint: Decides which providers and tools may see the data.
review.publishers: An agent engineer reviews the draft and publishes it (roles: {roles}).
review.toolApprovers: Steps marked for approval wait for a human at run time (roles: {roles}).
review.copyForEngineer: Copy agents.md for your agent engineer

events.title: Events & sources
events.subtitle: Where events come from: webhooks, mail-in, Kafka topics and schedules.
events.noInboundText: Create a webhook source to receive signed events from other systems.
events.noKafkaText: Kafka consumers are configured on the control node (SASL/TLS).
events.cronText: Schedules are declared as cron triggers in agents.md and become active with the published version.
events.noEventsText: Send a signed test request to an ingest URL to see it here.
events.matchingTriggers: all agents with a matching trigger
events.howToSign: How do I sign a request?
events.signText: Compute an HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body with the secret that the reference points to and send it as x-oax-signature. The secret itself never appears in the UI.
events.subject: Subject

form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Lowercase slug; agents reference it in their triggers, e.g. “jira”.
form.secretRefHint: Name of the environment variable or Kubernetes secret – never the secret value.

runs.title: Runs
runs.subtitle: Every execution of an agent, step by step – policy-checked, audited and cost-tracked.
runs.emptyText: Runs appear when an event triggers an agent or someone starts a test run.
runs.cancelText: The worker stops before the next step. Already executed tool calls are not undone.
runs.noSteps: No steps yet – the run is waiting for a worker.
runs.outputsPending: Outputs appear when the run finishes.

handover.invalid: The {direction} does not match its schema ({count} violations). Values are never logged.
handover.missing: The {direction} needs the output of a step that did not run.
handover.retry: The output was invalid; asking the agent once more.

approvals.noPermission: You can't decide on approvals (permission runs:approve).

connections.title: Connections
connections.subtitle: MCP servers and APIs that agents may use – provided by integrators.
connections.secretsNotice: Secrets are referenced by name only (envSecrets, headerSecrets, apiKeySecret) and are never shown or stored here.
connections.emptyText: Add an MCP server so agents can use its tools.
connections.configHint: JSON. Use envSecrets / headerSecrets with secret names instead of values.
connections.name: Name
connections.nameHint: Lowercase slug; agents.md refers to it as “server”.
connections.deleteText: Agents that use this connection will fail their tool calls until it is added again.
connections.scopeHint: Platform connections are available to every tenant and managed by the platform operator.

profiles.title: Tool access and profiles
profiles.hint: Classify each tool as read or write (undeclared tools count as write), then group tools into named profiles such as read or write. Agents grant a profile (for example jira:read); read-only steps can never receive a write tool.
profiles.problems: These profile entries will be refused: {items}

connections.proposeHint: Bring your own key: reference the key by secret name. Prices are proposed from the pinned model catalog and can be overridden per model.
connections.invalidJson: The configuration is not valid JSON.
connections.inlineSecret: Looks like a secret value at {paths}. Reference secrets by name instead.

policies.title: Policies
policies.subtitle: Guardrails checked before every tool call and while runs execute.
policies.gateText: Before each tool call the deterministic policy engine checks the agent's allowlist and argument constraints from agents.md plus these policies. Violations are blocked and logged.
policies.controlText: Watches running agents against budgets, rates, data classification and forbidden actions; can pause or stop a run.
policies.emptyText: Add a policy to forbid tools or argument patterns for all agents.
policies.name: Name
policies.globHint: One glob per line over server/tool, e.g. */delete_* or shell/*
policies.patternHint: One regular expression per line, optionally “pattern | reason”.
policies.budgetsText: Per-run budgets live in agents.md; monthly budgets are set per team. Runs stop hard when a budget is reached.

tester.title: Try the audit gate
tester.text: Checks a hypothetical tool call against an agent's draft and the active policies – nothing is executed.
tester.invalidJson: The arguments are not valid JSON.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.subtitle: Append-only, hash-chained record of everything that happened.
audit.verifyDetails: {entries} entries and {checkpoints} signed checkpoints checked; head is #{seq}.
audit.verifyDetailsEmpty: {entries} entries and {checkpoints} signed checkpoints checked; the trail is empty.

costs.title: Costs
costs.subtitle: Tokens and cost per run, agent, team and month.
costs.emptyText: Costs are recorded per step as soon as runs call a model.
costs.monthlyBudgetsText: Runs stop hard as soon as a budget is reached, also in the middle of a run. Alerts are raised at 50, 80 and 100 %.
costs.budgetInvalid: Enter a use case and a limit of 0 or more.

users.title: Users & teams
users.subtitle: Who may do what: roles per user, scoped globally or per team.
users.name: Name
users.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. LDAP and OIDC users sign in with their directory account.
users.noTeamsText: Teams own agents and budgets and scope role bindings.
users.matrixText: Which permissions each role grants. Team bindings limit them to that team's resources.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.subtitle: Tokens for machines and scripts – hashed, scoped and expiring.
tokens.emptyText: Create a token to call the API from CI or scripts.
tokens.revokeText: Clients using this token lose access immediately.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.scopeHint: Grant only what the client needs. A token never has more permissions than its owner.
tokens.showOnce: Copy the token now – it is shown only once and stored only as a hash.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Capabilities of this control node. Server settings are configured via environment / Helm values.
settings.providersText: Configured providers and the highest data classification each may receive.
settings.runnersText: Where runs execute. Container and Kubernetes workers follow in v0.2, Lambda and CI runners in v0.3.

bedrock.title: AWS Bedrock via VPC endpoint or proxy
bedrock.text: Build the provider entry for OAX_PROVIDERS (or the Helm value providers). Traffic stays inside your VPC when you set the interface endpoint.
bedrock.name: Provider name
bedrock.endpointHint: The bedrock-runtime endpoint DNS name of your VPC interface endpoint.
bedrock.credentials: Credentials come from the AWS default chain (IRSA on EKS, instance role) – never from this page.

welcome.title: Welcome to the open-agentix demo
welcome.body: You are signed in as the fictional demo admin. All data is fake and read-only, runs use a simulated provider, and nothing you type ever reaches a model. The demo resets nightly.

scenario.title: Try a scenario
scenario.body: This card starts one of a few fixed scenarios: a CVE-triage agent works through a scanner finding. Close the tour and press "Run scenario" whenever you like; you cannot type prompts.

runs.title: Watch a run
runs.body: Every run lists its steps, the policy decision for each tool call, approvals that wait for a human and the cost of each step. Open any run to see the full timeline.

audit.title: A tamper-evident audit trail
audit.body: Every action is written to a hash chain: each entry contains the hash of the one before it. The verify button re-computes the chain, so a changed or deleted entry is detected.

costs.title: Costs you can attribute
costs.body: Spend is tracked per agent, per use case and per tenant, with budgets and an export. The demo prices are illustrative; the simulated provider is free.

agents.title: Agents, tenants and roles
agents.body: Agents belong to teams inside tenants. People get roles per tenant, per team or even per single agent, so a contractor can see one agent and nothing else.

connections.title: Connections, tool profiles and policies
connections.body: MCP connections define which tools exist, tool profiles pick the few an agent may use, and policies decide each call. The default is least privilege: what is not allowed is denied.

links.title: Where to go next
links.body: Read the docs, browse the code or ask questions at info@openagentix.si or in GitHub Discussions. You can restart this tour any time with "Take the tour" in the sidebar.

plans.title: Agent plans
plans.subtitle: Paste or upload a plan and check it for least privilege. The result is advisory: nothing is saved or published here.
plans.sourceHint: At most 64 KiB. The plan is data and is never executed.
plans.tooLarge: The file is larger than 64 KiB.
plans.noFindings: No findings. The plan follows the least-privilege rules.
plans.advisory: The checks are advisory. An agent engineer still reviews every draft before it is published.
plans.draftNote: A draft only. It is saved when you create the agent in the editor.
plans.openEditor: Open in the new agent editor
plans.noDraftText: The plan has error findings. Fix them and generate the draft again.
